chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid. He said:

I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of God, inform me about the Quran — is it the Creator, or is it created? So he said: It is not the Creator, nor is it created, but rather it is the Word of God.

key_terms.خَالِق: Creator — one who brings into existence from nothing; a divine attribute. Calling the Quran 'khaliq' would imply it is God Himself.
key_terms.كَلَامُ اللَّه: The Word of God — the Shia theological designation for the Quran, affirming its divine origin without equating it with God's essence
key_terms.مَخْلُوق: Created — that which has been brought into existence; a temporal being. The Mu'tazilites held the Quran to be created ('khalq al-Quran').

ai.seo_question: Is the Quran created or uncreated according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Al-Husayn ibn Khalid asked Imam al-Rida (AS) about the status of the Quran in the long-standing theological dispute: is it the Creator (i.e., divine) or is it created (as the Mu'tazilites insisted)? The Imam articulated the Shia theological position that the Quran belongs to neither category — it is neither a second deity nor a temporal creation, but is the eternal Word (kalam) of God. This position distinguished Shia theology from both Ash'ari and Mu'tazili schools on the question of the Quran's nature.
